note: Establishes narrator voice and move-in; introduces the locket as an inciting curiosity/object; sets domestic texture (smell, clock, mirror).
Discovery scene: physical items in the attic (doll, diary, chalk marks, stash under floorboard) escalate the physical evidence and suggest a child's presence; moves plot toward investigation.
Methodical, physical corroboration: sepia date, locket initial similarity, stain matches diary fragment; Mrs. Hollis's evasions raise tension and possible obstruction.
Confrontation produces confession and a tangible release: the ghost's repetitive signs quieten and a concealment is confessed. This advances the arc toward closure of the house's earlier mystery.
